title: Dental X-ray
what: This is a small X-ray of one or a few teeth. It shows decay between teeth and the state of the root.
why: To find hidden decay and check the roots, fillings, and bone around a tooth.
duration: usually 1 to 5 minutes; the image is ready right away
tell_doctor: If you are or might be pregnant

prepare.title: Jewelry
prepare.text: Remove earrings, mouth piercings, and removable dentures if asked.

bring: Your referral, if you have one
steps: You sit in the chair and may get a protective apron
A small sensor or film is placed in your mouth behind the teeth
You bite on a holder and keep still
The machine takes the image in a split second
The sensor comes out, and the image appears on screen
feel: The sensor in your mouth is a little uncomfortable
Some people gag. Breathe through your nose
after: The dentist looks at the image right away and tells you what is next

faq.a: The radiation dose is very small. The X-ray is taken when it is needed for treatment.

faq.q: Can I have it while pregnant?
faq.a: If it is needed, it is done with protection. Be sure to tell your dentist you are pregnant.

reminders.text: Dental X-ray in an hour. Bring your ID.
